pairs.subject: streaming-platform-api-custody
pairs.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-types/src/rpc.rs:621 The disconnect RPC returns the generic ModeratorStatus (state + free-text detail), so the wire contract has no field for 'revocation unconfirmed' or 'purge verified'; the console cannot show the streamer which teardown steps the platform actually confirmed.

techniques.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-types/src/moderation.rs:221 TwitchConnect carries only verification_uri, user_code and expires_s, and PlatformStatus only bot_login/channel/detail. No contract type or RPC result carries an access or refresh token. Caveat: ModDecision reports outcomes as executed: bool plus error: Option<String> (moderation.rs:95/101), not as typed done/refused/rate-limited/unknown classes.
crates/shadowrunr-types/src/rpc.rs:621 The disconnect result has no typed revoked/unconfirmed/purged/stopped report, so an unconfirmed revocation can never reach the caller as a state.

crates/shadowrunr-types/src/moderation.rs:119 The moderation log has only Decision and Unban variants. Neither it, PlatformStatus nor StreamEvent has a gap entry with both edges, so a period of dropped platform events cannot be recorded as 'unseen'.

crates/shadowrunr-types/src/moderation.rs:101 This crate does no rate limiting; the broker (daemon helix.rs) fails fast on a 429. The reset moment reaches the contract only as free text in error, never as a typed rate-limited-until value, so the console cannot show a countdown.
crates/shadowrunr-types/src/moderation.rs:222 Refresh and device-code polling live in the daemon broker. The contract only carries the device code's expiry, which lets the UI stop at the deadline.

pairs.registryProposal: For a shared wire-contract crate, the standard could state what the contract must carry: a typed broker outcome class (done / refused / rate_limited_until / unauthorised / unknown), a gap event with both edges, and a typed disconnect report. Without that, a conformant broker's honesty is lost at the RPC boundary.
